title: ToolApiV1
description: K-09 Tool API v1, DRAFT (T-009; not frozen: T-018 freezes it with journeys 1 and 2). The calls that own every read and write (arch 02 line 139): the turn face (called by the handle actor and the AI layer) and the shared core (M3b: the any-time rows every chat needs from its first text). The same calls serve texts, secure pages and outside AIs under the same limits; free text from pages and AIs gets the safety read first (arch 02 line 129); row-level security per business on every call (arch 10 line 546). There is no root payload: each payload is one definition under $defs, named <call>.request, <call>.response and <call>.errors. contracts/tool-api/README.md states each call's read, repeat safety and time budget.

nullableUtc.title: NullableUtc
nullableUtc.description: An instant in UTC, or null (CQ-09).

fixedLineId.title: FixedLineId
fixedLineId.description: A fixed line's id in the pinned bundle, such as optOutLine or stopLaterReply (K-01 v1 fixedLine.id; arch 07 line 361: fixed lines go word for word).

caller.title: Caller
caller.description: Who makes a call, under which business, and the key a repeat is known by. Every request carries it (arch 02 lines 129, 139; arch 10 line 546).

kind.description: Who calls: turn (the handle actor's turn, through gateAndCommit; arch 02 line 121), page (a secure page or the portal, through K-21), agent (an outside AI through the Agent API, K-20), console (the team console, C-194), job (an offline or queue job, such as the dispatcher or a calendar renewal), clockFiring (a clock row's firing with no handle, the minute sweep's: arch 10 line 540) or actorOnReturn (a line the handle actor sent while PostgreSQL was down, written on return: arch 11 line 566). The same calls serve texts, secure pages and outside AIs under the same limits (arch 02 line 129).

turnId.description: For kind turn, the turn whose one commit carries the call (arch 02 line 121; arch 10 line 508); null otherwise.

requestId.description: The caller's own id for this request: the key a repeat is known by when no turn carries the call (a page or agent request id, a console tap, a job run or a clock row id). For kind turn, the turn id again.

businessId.description: The business the call runs under: row-level security scopes every Tool API call by it (arch 10 line 546; K-04 v1 rule 4). Null only where no business exists yet, or for a call that covers every business (a STOP: RULES 7.2).

personId.description: The person the caller acts for, when known: the sender of the turn's texts, the signed-in person on a page, the customer an agent token is bound to, or the team member at the console (limit 1: arch 06 line 299).

traceId.description: The trace the call joins (K-08 v1; arch 10 line 548): each call adds its span (hops frontier, search, gate, commit, compose, fillAndChecks, rewriteOrFallback, pageRequest, agentApiRequest).

sentByActor.description: A line the handle actor already sent straight through Linq while PostgreSQL was down: written on return, never sent again (arch 11 line 566; QUESTIONS.md NQ-RT-9's default: with PostgreSQL up, the line is an outbox row). Null when the call writes the row to be sent.

at.description: When the actor sent it (arch 11 line 566).

fixedLineId.description: The checked line it sent from its local copy (C-053).

linqMessageId.description: Linq's message id for the send, so the row written on return matches it (K-07 v1 outbox parts).

notAllowedError.title: NotAllowedError
notAllowedError.description: Limit 1 or row-level security refused the caller: a change that adds a person, a way in, money or authority needs the decider's own yes (arch 06 line 299; S13-45), and no call reads or writes another business's rows (arch 10 line 546). Nothing was written.

why.description: notDecider: the caller is not the person who decides (the person served or who decides for them; the owner or a permitted admin for fees, refunds beyond the terms, team and settings: arch 06 line 299); unprovenSender: the sender is not yet proven (a proof code goes first: proveCode); wrongRole: the step is not this role's (S11-12 and S11-42 are the owner's); otherBusiness: the row is another business's (arch 10 line 546).

bookingPausedError.title: BookingPausedError
bookingPausedError.description: PostgreSQL is down: agents and the booking page hear that booking is paused (arch 11 line 566; S12-12). Nothing was written; the caller may try again later. Q-45's default: nothing covers an outage of Cloudflare itself, so this answer exists only while the Workers run.

retryAfterSeconds.description: When the caller may try again, in seconds. No source gives the number: the runtime sets it (README open gaps).

turnParkedError.title: TurnParkedError
turnParkedError.description: The turn was parked after a third crash before its commit and never commits (arch 11 line 576; K-05 v1 parkTurn).

gateOutcome.description: What a failed limit does to its choice (arch 02 line 121: 'A failed limit runs its own outcome and stops only its choice and what depends on it'): ask (Rosie asks one question now and the choice waits for its answer as an open question), refuse (the choice ends: nothing is saved, and Rosie says why) or wait (the choice is held, nothing committed for it, until something outside this turn happens: a code typed back, a person, a safety hold's release). Each limit's own outcomes are listed in limit1Outcome to limit6Outcome.

limit1Outcome.title: Limit1Outcome
limit1Outcome.description: Limit 1's outcome when it fails (arch 06 line 299). Each action has one kind of outcome (gateOutcome): proofCodeSent is wait; askedDecider is ask.

action.description: Unproven sender: a code to the contact on file, in words that never confirm a booking exists (arch 06 line 299; RULES 6.2); the choice waits for the code typed back within 10 minutes (proveCode).
Wrong person: a question in the decider's own chat (arch 06 line 299; S13-45).

limit2Outcome.title: Limit2Outcome
limit2Outcome.description: Limit 2's outcome when it fails (arch 06 line 301). Each action has one kind of outcome (gateOutcome): saidWhatRuleAllows is refuse.

action.description: Rosie says what the rule allows; nothing is saved (arch 06 line 301).

limit3Outcome.title: Limit3Outcome
limit3Outcome.description: Limit 3's outcome when it fails (arch 06 line 303). Each action has one kind of outcome (gateOutcome): freshReadBack is ask; safeDefault is refuse.

action.description: A fresh read-back, once (arch 06 line 303; S13-25 rules 16 to 18).
After the fresh read-back, still no exact yes: the step's safe default, and the owner is told (arch 06 line 303).

limit4Outcome.title: Limit4Outcome
limit4Outcome.description: Limit 4's outcome when it fails (arch 06 line 305; K-05 v1 commitTurn versionChanged). Each action has one kind of outcome (gateOutcome): freshYes is ask; saidWhatChanged is refuse; toPerson is wait.

limit.description: Limit 4: Versions (arch 06 line 305). The gate reloads once first; nothing shown changed means the choice commits and the limit passes.

action.description: Changed but still possible: today's facts and a fresh yes (arch 06 line 305).

limit.description: Limit 4: Versions (arch 06 line 305). The gate reloads once first; nothing shown changed means the choice commits and the limit passes.

action.description: No longer possible: say what changed and offer the current choices (arch 06 line 305).

limit.description: Limit 4: Versions (arch 06 line 305). The gate reloads once first; nothing shown changed means the choice commits and the limit passes.

action.description: A second conflict on one question: a person (arch 06 line 305).

limit5Outcome.title: Limit5Outcome
limit5Outcome.description: Limit 5's outcome when it fails (arch 06 line 307; K-05 v1 commitTurn reservationLost). Each action has one kind of outcome (gateOutcome): nextOpenTimes is ask; nothingBooked is refuse.

action.description: No pick in 10 minutes on the page, or 2 of their text hours otherwise: nothing booked (arch 06 line 307; A6-11).

limit6Outcome.title: Limit6Outcome
limit6Outcome.description: Limit 6's outcome when it fails (arch 06 line 309). Each action has one kind of outcome (gateOutcome): oneQuestion is ask; nothingChanged is refuse.

limit.description: Limit 6: Values (arch 06 line 309). The one Sonnet re-read is decide's and has run before the gate (arch 02 line 119; K-02 v1 decideResult.reread).

action.description: After the re-read, one question (arch 06 line 309).

limit.description: Limit 6: Values (arch 06 line 309). The one Sonnet re-read is decide's and has run before the gate (arch 02 line 119; K-02 v1 decideResult.reread).

action.description: Still failing after the question: nothing changes (arch 06 line 309).

limitOutcome.title: LimitOutcome
limitOutcome.description: The failed limit (1 to 6, checked before the commit) and its outcome (arch 06 lines 295 to 309; arch 02 line 121).

guardTargets.title: GuardTargets
guardTargets.description: What the guard listed for the handle: its roles, open questions and bookings (arch 02 line 115). The guard reads them through K-05 v1.2's state reads (T-072); this call takes them as given.

roles.description: The handle's roles per business (arch 02 line 115).

role.description: The role as K-04 v1 person_roles names it (FS line 723).

openQuestionIds.description: Every open question sent to this handle (arch 03 line 159; S13-12).

noTarget.description: true when nothing fits as a target: the doors are offered (arch 02 line 115; arch 03 line 165). No business named yet: search first; named-only work gets one ask for a name (S13-20).

buildFrontier.request.title: BuildFrontierRequest
buildFrontier.request.description: Build the frontier: the turn, its targets from the guard and the pinned bundle give K-02 v1's context (choices, cards, facts with their row versions, the rules prefix by hash, the last 6 messages). Each fact comes once from its one home (S13-30); a second value for one key is refused, the home's value goes in and the step is flagged for a fix (arch 02 line 117; arch 03 lines 157 to 167). Over 60 choices, each booking other than the target collapses to one 'which booking?' choice (arch 03 line 167). Reads: the primary, uncached (decision reads: arch 02 line 117; arch 10 lines 504, 538), and the pinned bundle from KV (its PostgreSQL copy on a miss: arch 10 line 536). Repeat: safe: a read; it writes nothing (a flagged step is reported in the response and on the frontier span). Time budget: at most 150 ms (arch 04 line 215: 'Build the frontier (uncached reads)').

turn.description: The turn as K-05 v1 will commit it: its id, handle, event ids, pinned bundle, trace ids and tries.

texts.description: The turn's texts after the edge scrub, in order (K-02 v1 text).

now.description: The time the turn reads 'now' at (the fake clock on staging: BP 9.4).

buildFrontier.response.title: BuildFrontierResponse
buildFrontier.response.description: The context for decide, with what the builder flagged or collapsed.

context.description: K-02 v1's context bundle, passed to decide unchanged (CQ-25 settled: the AI gateway's two calls a read are the wire form, not the Tool API's).

flagged.description: Steps flagged for a fix: a second value for one key was refused and the home's value went in (arch 02 line 117; this closes nm01).

key.description: The fact key that had a second value (arch 02 line 117).

kept.description: The home's row and version whose value went in (S13-30).

collapsedBookingIds.description: Bookings other than the target collapsed to one 'which booking?' choice because the frontier passed 60 (arch 03 line 167); empty when none.

buildFrontier.errors.title: BuildFrontierErrors
buildFrontier.errors.description: Refused, nothing written: buildFrontier's errors. Each is a JSON object with its own "error" code (02-contracts section 2 item 2).

oneOf.title: BundleNotFoundError
oneOf.description: The pinned bundle is in neither KV nor its PostgreSQL copy (arch 10 line 536; K-05 v1 readBundleValue).

oneOf.title: TooManyChoicesError
oneOf.description: Still over 60 choices after every other booking collapsed (arch 01 line 69: never more than 60). A builder fault: the turn takes the outage path (arch 06 line 293).

closestEntries.request.title: ClosestEntriesRequest
closestEntries.request.description: Add the closest entries when nothing fits: meaning search over this business's step graph adds the 3 closest entry steps as choices of kind searchEntry, and the turn's one re-read runs on them (arch 03 line 189; K-02 v1 context.meaningSearch). The model or index is Q-42's (a spike picks it). Reads: the pinned bundle and the meaning-match index (Q-42); the facts an added entry needs are read as buildFrontier reads them, on the primary, uncached. Repeat: safe: a read; the same context gives the same entries. Once per turn: a second call for one turn is refused (searchedAlready). Time budget: none in the sources. Proposed: at most 200 ms, the budget of 'Search, one indexed query' (arch 04 line 217, DD), since it is one indexed query (README default 3).

context.description: The turn's context as buildFrontier gave it (K-02 v1).

quotes.description: The parts of the text nothing fit, each by its exact quote (arch 03 line 185).

items.description: A quote of a part nothing fit (K-02 v1 noneFits).

closestEntries.response.title: ClosestEntriesResponse
closestEntries.response.description: The context with the closest entries added.

context.description: The same context with at most 3 entry steps added as choices of kind searchEntry and meaningSearch set (K-02 v1).

added.description: The entry steps added, closest first (arch 03 line 189).

closestEntries.errors.title: ClosestEntriesErrors
closestEntries.errors.description: Refused, nothing written: closestEntries's errors. Each is a JSON object with its own "error" code (02-contracts section 2 item 2).

oneOf.title: SearchedAlreadyError
oneOf.description: Meaning search already ran for this turn (arch 03 line 189: the turn's one re-read).

oneOf.title: IndexUnavailableError
oneOf.description: The meaning-match index cannot be read: the turn goes on to the planner with no entries added (arch 03 line 189). Q-42 is open.

plannerVerbs.request.title: PlannerVerbsRequest
plannerVerbs.request.description: The planner's verbs: answer from stored facts, ask one question, pass a question on, hand to a person, or log a gap case (arch 06 line 291). Never a booking, charge, refund, cancel, move or a change to a setting, contact or consent. Carried inside gateAndCommit.request.input.planner, because a turn commits once (arch 02 line 121); never called on its own. Every such turn is a gap case (arch 03 line 189; K-37 v1 gap_cases). Reads: the primary, uncached, inside the turn's commit. Repeat: as gateAndCommit, by the turn id. Time budget: inside gateAndCommit's 300 ms.

output.description: The Sonnet planner's output, one of its five verbs (K-02 v1; arch 06 line 291).

parts.description: The parts nothing fit, after meaning search (arch 03 line 189).

plannerVerbs.response.title: PlannerVerbsResponse
plannerVerbs.response.description: What the planner's verb committed in the turn's commit.

verb.description: The verb committed (K-02 v1 plannerOutput; K-37 v1 gap_cases.outcome).

outboxRowIds.description: The outbox rows the verb wrote: the answer, the question, the pass-on or the hand-off's alert.

openQuestionId.description: For ask, the open question; a reply to it that fits nothing goes to a person (S13-29 rule 54).

handOffId.description: For hand_off about another matter, the hand-off row (K-36 v1 hand_offs).

harmReportId.description: For hand_off about the owner or staff, the harm report Rosie's team follows up that day, never told to the person named (K-34 v1 harm_reports; arch 06 line 329).

gapCaseTurnId.description: The gap case logged for this turn (K-37 v1 gap_cases.turn_id: one per turn).

oneOf.description: Code refused the planner's output: an answer naming a fact the context does not hold, or an ask with more than one question (K-02 v1 README: code checks; C-092). The part takes the passed-on path: 'I've passed this on.' (arch 02 line 123).

partResult.title: PartResult
partResult.description: What the gate did with one part: committed, or the failed limit (1 to 6) and its outcome, which stops only that choice and what depends on it (arch 02 line 121; arch 06 lines 295 to 309).

part.description: The part's index in the decide result's parts (K-02 v1 decideResult.parts).

choiceId.description: The choice the part chose or entered (K-02 v1 choose or enter), or null for another verb.

result.description: committed: every limit passed and the choice's effects went in the commit (arch 02 line 121); stopped: a limit failed and ran its own outcome (stoppedBy); dependsOnStopped: it depends on a stopped choice, so it stops too (arch 02 line 121); held: a safety outcome holds the turn's routine actions (arch 06 lines 315 to 327; K-34 v1 safety_holds); asked: decide ended it in one question, nothing changed (K-02 v1 resultPart oneQuestion); noAction: a verb that commits nothing for it (no_op, redact, or a none_fits the planner took).

limits.description: Each of limits 1 to 6 with its result (pass, fail or notChecked), as the gate span logs them (K-08 v1 limitResult).

stoppedBy.description: For stopped, the limit that failed and its outcome; null otherwise.

dependsOnPart.description: For dependsOnStopped, the part it depends on; null otherwise.

anyOf.description: The index of the stopped part it depends on.

gateAndCommit.request.title: GateAndCommitRequest
gateAndCommit.request.description: Gate and commit a turn: the gate checks limits 1 to 6 on the agreed parts with their quotes; code adds each choice's effects; one transaction writes state, one outbox row per message (no plan yet), clock rows, effect rows and the event log under the turn id (arch 02 line 121; arch 06 lines 295 to 309; arch 10 line 508). It commits through K-05 v1 commitTurn, or for a clock's firing through K-05 v1 fireClock (QUESTIONS.md NQ-RT-4); effect rows and the waiting rows' moves (K-07 v1 waiting_chat to superseded or withdrawn) are K-05 v1.1's (T-071). A limit 4 or 5 refusal from the commit reloads once and gates again (arch 06 line 305). Reads: the primary, uncached (arch 02 line 117; arch 10 lines 504, 508). Repeat: safe: the turn id is the key; a repeat writes nothing and returns the first commit with repeated true (K-05 v1 commitTurn; tour line 418). Time budget: at most 300 ms (arch 04 line 223: 'Gate and commit').

turn.description: The turn row the commit writes (K-05 v1 turn). For a clock's firing, the firing's turn (K-05 v1 fireClock.request.turn).

input.description: What the turn acts on: decided texts, a clock's firing, or only core actions (the guard's keyword-only texts: arch 02 line 115).

decided.description: The context and decide's result, as the gate reads them (K-02 v1 contextAndDecide; its named rules are the gate's: optionOffered, quoteInText).

planner.description: The planner's verb when nothing fit after meaning search; null otherwise.

oneOf.title: ClockInput
oneOf.description: A clock's firing runs its branch with no decide reads (QUESTIONS.md NQ-RT-4; arch 02 line 127).

clockRowId.description: The clock row firing (K-05 v1 fireClock).

by.description: As K-05 v1 fireClock.request.by: the actor's alarm, the minute sweep, or staging's Fire now (BP 9.4).

jobId.description: The firing's job id for the event log (K-05 v1 fireClock).

oneOf.title: CoreOnlyInput
oneOf.description: Only core actions: STOP, START, HELP and the like, which code alone acts on (arch 02 line 115).

core.description: Shared-core calls this turn commits, in order (README 'In a turn or alone'). Each of the turn's texts carries one recordSafetyOutcome, whatever its outcome, since K-34 v1 writes one outcome row per text under the turn that joins it (README default 5); a clock's turn carries none.

now.description: The time the gate reads 'now' at.

gateAndCommit.response.title: GateAndCommitResponse
gateAndCommit.response.description: Committed: per part either committed or the failed limit and its outcome, and what the one commit wrote.

repeated.description: true when this turn id had committed before: nothing was written and the first commit comes back (K-05 v1 commitTurn).

parts.description: One result per decide part, in order; empty for a clock's or a core-only turn.

planner.description: The planner's verb as committed, or null.

core.description: One result per core action, in the request's order.

written.description: What the commit wrote: rows with their versions, outbox rows in commit order, promotions (K-05 v1).

effects.description: Effect rows written in the commit, to run after it (K-07 v1 effect rows; written through K-05 v1.1's commit, T-071). Empty until K-05 v1.1 freezes.

effectId.description: The effect id reconciliation matches by (arch 10 line 550).

closed.description: Open questions closed (answered, defaulted or withdrawn).

gateAndCommit.errors.title: GateAndCommitErrors
gateAndCommit.errors.description: Refused, nothing written: gateAndCommit's errors. Each is a JSON object with its own "error" code (02-contracts section 2 item 2).

oneOf.title: BundleMismatchError
oneOf.description: The context or decide result names another bundle than the turn's pinned one (arch 10 line 548: the bundle id is on every turn). Nothing was written.

oneOf.title: DecideRefusedError
oneOf.description: The decide result breaks a K-02 v1 named rule: a choice the context did not offer (optionOffered; arch 06 line 333) or a quote not found in the turn's texts (quoteInText; arch 03 line 185). Nothing was written; the AI layer treats it as a failed read (arch 06 line 293).

composeInput.request.title: ComposeInputRequest
composeInput.request.description: Compose input: for one committed outbox row, K-03 v1's composer input, with its committed choices and only what limit 7 lets its recipient see, never the frontier (arch 07 line 397). An email copy takes its text row's plan instead, so it gets no composer input (arch 07 line 397). After a crash only rows without a plan are composed (arch 11 line 576). Reads: the primary, uncached: the row and today's record (limit 7 reads what this recipient may see: arch 06 line 311). Repeat: safe: a read. Time budget: none in the sources; it sits inside 'Write the reply, or one rewrite: 2–3 s' (arch 04 line 225).

outboxRowId.description: The committed outbox row (K-04 v1 outbox_rows; K-07 v1 state planned or stale).

composeInput.response.title: ComposeInputResponse
composeInput.response.description: The composer input, or the text row an email copy takes its plan from.

textRowId.description: The text row whose plan the copy reuses (K-03 v1 rowPlan.copyOf; RULES 4.1).

composeInput.errors.title: ComposeInputErrors
composeInput.errors.description: Refused, nothing written: composeInput's errors. Each is a JSON object with its own "error" code (02-contracts section 2 item 2).

oneOf.title: AlreadyPlannedError
oneOf.description: The row already holds a plan: nothing to compose (arch 11 line 576; K-05 v1 writePlan alreadyPlanned).

oneOf.title: RowClosedError
oneOf.description: The row is no longer to be sent (K-07 v1: dropped_stopped, withdrawn, superseded or failed): nothing is composed.

finalizeMessage.request.title: FinalizeMessageRequest
finalizeMessage.request.description: Finalize a message: for an outbox row and its plan, code inserts the options word for word, adds the fixed lines, fills the slots, runs the claim check (limit 7) and the message checks (arch 02 line 123; arch 07 lines 405 to 417). Every check passed, or only shape, length and reading after the one rewrite: the final parts are written with the plan (K-05 v1 writePlan; K-07 v1 planned to checked). A blocking miss on the composed plan: the failed checks come back for the one rewrite. A blocking miss on the rewrite: code fills the step's fallback text (Jay's reviewed one, or its master line with slots filled) through the same checks; none passes: 'I've passed this on. Rosie's team will reply within 1 business day.', the question withdrawn so no clock arms (K-05 v1 cancelClock with withdrawQuestion; RULES 5.2), and the team paged (pageTeam, reason passed_on). Reads: the primary, uncached: the row, its slots' values and the reader's audience (limit 7: arch 06 line 311). Repeat: safe: a row with a plan keeps it; a repeat answers alreadyPlanned with the stored final parts (K-05 v1 writePlan). Time budget: none in the sources; the checks are code, inside 'Write the reply, or one rewrite: 2–3 s' (arch 04 line 225).

expectVersion.description: The row's version when its input was composed (limit 4 at the write: K-05 v1 writePlan).

attempt.description: composed: the composer's plan; rewrite: the one rewrite, told what failed (K-03 v1 checkResult.attempt). The fallback is code's, run inside this call.

plan.description: The plan as the row will store it (K-03 v1 rowPlan).

finalizeMessage.response.title: FinalizeMessageResponse
finalizeMessage.response.description: The check results and what was written.

outcome.description: send: every check passed and the final parts are written; sendAndLog: only shape, length and reading or format missed after the one rewrite, written and logged (arch 07 line 417); rewrite: a miss on the composed plan, nothing written, the composer gets one rewrite told what failed; passedOn: the rewrite and the fallback both failed (arch 02 line 123).

checks.description: Each attempt's check result, in order: the attempt sent, then the fallback when code ran it (K-03 v1 checkResult).

finalParts.description: The final parts written, or null for rewrite.

questionWithdrawn.description: true for passedOn: the question is withdrawn, so no clock arms (RULES 5.2).

teamPageId.description: For passedOn, the page to Rosie's team (K-36 v1 team_pages reason passed_on); null otherwise.

finalizeMessage.errors.title: FinalizeMessageErrors
finalizeMessage.errors.description: Refused, nothing written: finalizeMessage's errors. Each is a JSON object with its own "error" code (02-contracts section 2 item 2).

oneOf.title: FinalizeAlreadyPlannedError
oneOf.description: The row already holds a plan and final parts (K-05 v1 writePlan alreadyPlanned): they come back unchanged.

oneOf.title: RewriteUsedError
oneOf.description: The one rewrite was already checked for this row (arch 07 line 417: one rewrite).

oneOf.title: FinalizeRowClosedError
oneOf.description: The row is no longer to be sent (K-07 v1 rowState).

recordSafetyOutcome.request.title: RecordSafetyOutcomeRequest
recordSafetyOutcome.request.description: Record a safety outcome and its holds (arch 06 lines 315 to 329; A3-22 to A3-26, A3-48 to A3-50, B3-17): the outcome row (K-34 v1 safety_outcomes, one per text, No included), the hold with its release rule (safety_holds: at once, when private, after a clear 'we're safe', or never), the outcome step's checked line as an outbox row of send class safety, at any hour, past any opt-out (arch 02 line 111; NQ-RT-9), and who is told (arch 06 line 329): crisis words, the owner and Rosie's team at once; an emergency or a threat, the owner, then after 5 minutes whoever they named and Rosie's team (handOff); harm to a child or older adult, or a report about the owner or staff, Rosie's team that day (K-34 v1 harm_reports). For a text it rides in the commit of the turn its text joins (gateAndCommit core; README default 5); for free text from a page or an outside AI it is called alone, and danger returns the safety message to the caller and nothing books (arch 02 line 129). Reads: the primary, uncached. Repeat: safe: the text's event id (K-02 v1 safetyResult.eventId) is the key; one outcome row per text, and a repeat returns the first. Time budget: the checked line is sent first, within 5 s (QUESTIONS.md NQ-RT-9's default); the read itself is 2 s per model, 4 s in all (arch 02 line 111), the AI layer's.

The stop reply is C1's every-business reply (Q-01's words). Written on return when PostgreSQL was down: the actor sent the reply and keeps the stopped flag (arch 11 line 566).
